subject: Deployment pathway qualification & two-option sizing request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Quick recap + token mix worksheet and next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, Asha — good progress. Per our discussion I pulled together a short recap and a couple of asks so we can get a tight capacity recommendation for NextRetail's inference needs.

Summary from call:
- Primary workload: product description generation + light chat assistant used in checkout flows.
- Preferred deployment: leaning Dedicated capacity for predictable latency/cost; possibility of Private VPC later if PCI scope expands.
- Target steady-state: ~120 TPS at peak (text generation endpoint). Bursts: up to ~200 TPS during promotional spikes (5% of the hour).
- Concurrency goal: want ~6–10 concurrent requests per replica (you mentioned 8 as target).
- Token mix: we discussed short+medium+long buckets but I asked you to confirm distribution.
- Compliance/signing: procurement will need SOC2 evidence and a short SLA; you said you'd share your internal SLA/requirements doc.

Asks / action items:
1) Please attach the token-mix CSV with representative percent distribution (we use that to size batch / KV cache impact). I attached a blank worksheet (nextretail_token_mix.csv) below — if you can fill the 3 buckets (<=64, 65–512, >512) and an average prompt/response token estimate that would be ideal.
2) Confirm whether model will be a 7B/13B generative model (smaller) or a 70B+ family for retrieval-augmented generation (that materially changes GPU selection).
3) Any procurement constraints (PO process, billing contact, expected timeline). You mentioned procurement@nextretail.com — please CC them on replies.

Next steps from our side: once we have the CSV and model family, Karthik will propose two Dedicated sizing options (conservative and aggressive) and a quick note on when Private VPC would be recommended. We'll include estimated monthly cost buckets and a suggested autoscale policy.

Proposing a 30-minute follow-up call next Tue 10:00am PT to review the two options + procurement path. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: nextretail_token_mix.csv (worksheet)

—

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. Filling the worksheet now and adding a short note here so you have the numbers while the CSV is attached.

Traffic and tokens (representative):

- Burst: up to 200 TPS for short windows (~5–10 minutes during promos) roughly twice per week

- Token distribution (attached CSV): 70% <=64 tokens, 25% 65–512 tokens, 5% >512 tokens
- Average output tokens per request: ~80 tokens (prompt avg 40, completion 80 for product descriptions)

Model: we plan to start on a 13B open model (generation quality acceptable), but roadmap includes evaluating a 70B variant next quarter if quality/regression demands it. Please size for the 13B baseline and call out delta for 70B.

Compliance/procurement: attaching our procurement SLA doc (nextretail_sla_2027.pdf). Procurement timeline: PO in 2–3 weeks after commercial terms; billing contact is procurement@nextretail.com.

We are inclined to start on Dedicated for predictable latency and cost; Private VPC is a blocker only if we onboard payment card handling in the next 6 months — worth future-proofing but not required in the immediate POC.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap + token mix worksheet and next steps

Ben / Marissa — reviewed Asha's CSV and SLA. High-level recommendations below (13B baseline). I attached the SKU options PDF with cost buckets and assumptions.

Short answer: Dedicated pool makes sense for NextRetail. Two viable options: conservative (latency/SLO-first) and cost-optimized (smaller commit + autoscale).

Conservative (recommended for initial POC + promo headroom):
- Hardware: 4 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (dedicated instances, one model replica per GPU).
- Concurrency per replica: 8; Max batch size: 64; continuous batching enabled.
- Expected steady throughput: ~30 TPS per GPU at the given token mix and avg 80 tokens per request -> ~120 TPS total.
- Burst capacity: with autoscale policy (add 2 GPUs on sustained burst) covers the 200 TPS short spikes; warm-up + KV cache reduces cold penalty.
- KV/prefix caching: estimate ~20–30% compute reduction given 70% short-token requests and repeated prefixes in checkout flows.
- Cost: higher upfront reserved commitment; estimated monthly run-rate provided in attached PDF.

Aggressive / cost-optimized (lower commit, faster autoscale):
- Hardware: 6 x NVIDIA H100 (or cloud equivalent pooled, using smaller model replicas per GPU). H100 gives better perf for 13B/70B if you plan to move up to 70B soon.
- Concurrency per replica: 6–8; Max batch size: 96 for short requests (more efficient batching).
- Expected steady throughput: ~20 TPS per H100 (model + quantization dependent) -> ~120 TPS across pool but more efficient on per-token cost for medium/long requests.
- Burst handling: autoscale + pre-warmed spare capacity (1–2 GPUs) recommended for sub-minute promos.
- KV caching: similar 20% savings assumed if request patterns are cache-friendly.
- Notes on 70B delta: moving to 70B increases RAM and latency needs; estimate ~2–2.5x compute; H100 becomes strongly preferred for a 70B rollout.

Operational suggestions:
- Start with conservative A100 pool for POC to hit latency SLOs; create an autoscale policy that prefers adding GPUs rather than scaling down below 3 GPUs during business hours to avoid thrash.
- Enable prefix/KV cache and test a synthetic load from their token distribution; we can reduce pool size after observing cache hit rates.
- Suggested replica layout: 4 model replicas/shard (one per GPU) with 8 concurrent streams each; tune max_batch by observing tail-latency at 99th pct.

I attached redwood-dedicated-sku-options.pdf (two-option cost & assumptions). If useful, I can produce a quick cost model sheet with token-per-month inputs from procurement.

—
Karthik Iyer
Staff ML Infra Engineer

- Option B (Cost-optimized): 6x H100, higher efficiency on bursts and future 70B migration, slightly different autoscale profile; lower per-token cost for medium/long requests but more operational sensitivity during cold starts.
